securityFindings: CRITICAL: the ticket is never validated against anything SUBMISSION issued — no lookup, no expiry check, no single-use enforcement. Any non-empty string in X-Upload-Ticket is accepted. Combined with the endpoint URL being delivered to every visitor's browser, this is an unauthenticated write path into the agency's SharePoint registry.
No file size limit is enforced.
No integrity check (SHA-256 or otherwise) against any declared digest — triggerBody() is written to SharePoint unexamined.

No association is recorded between the stored file and the correspondence record it belongs to — the ticket is sanitized into a filename fragment, never decoded or looked up. Combined with the forced .bin extension and the absent original filename, a stored file has no machine- or human-readable link back to its submission, name, or real content type.

response.consumptionNote: support.js's send() calls PF.intake.support({...}) with no .then(), no assignment, no use of the returned promise. The reference shown to the citizen (ticket.ref) is generated by the local sref() function BEFORE PF.intake.support is even called, and is never reconciled with data.caseRef. Whatever the flow returns has zero effect on what the citizen sees.
